subject: How can I change the reference values in logistic regression?

messages.author: 66358fa675d5666d
messages.subject: How can I change the reference values in logistic regression?
parts:
Hello everybody,

I'm using the logistic regression model (lrm) from the design package (described in Ch. 5.4 of Stefan Gries's book) with binary independent variables like PENULT (=PU or NPU), FREQUENCY (=High or Low) and so on.

My question is: How I can change the reference values of each of these variables in lrm (i.e. the values that don't appear in the model output)?
In other words, in:

PENULT=PU                  2.1719 0.14288 15.20  0.0000
INTERF=NIF                 2.3856 0.13351 17.87  0.0000
SCHWA=NoHelp              -1.2486 0.12608 -9.90  0.0000
LEXNEIGH=NoFriend         -0.8557 0.08665 -9.88  0.0000
FREQUENCY=Low             -0.3451 0.12818 -2.69  0.0071
PENULT=PU * INTERF=NIF    -1.3266 0.18529 -7.16  0.0000
PENULT=PU * FREQUENCY=Low -0.5712 0.17234 -3.31  0.0009

how can I make appear PENULT=NPU, INTERF=IF and so on?
Thanks for your help,

Peter

P.S. Here's the complete screen output:

> library(Design)
> options(contrasts=c("contr.treatment", "contr.poly"))
> DAT<-read.table(choose.files(), header=TRUE, sep="\t", comment.char="", quote="")

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [StatForLing with R] How can I change the reference values in logistic regression?
parts:
You can use relevel to change the reference level to something else or
use Anova (car) to get overall p-values for a variable.

STG

messages.author: 3eece7b41f260fa7
messages.subject: Re: How can I change the reference values in logistic regression?
parts:
Hi, a very simple way to do it is to rename your values putting
figures before each value:

1PU, 2NPU => now PU will be automatically chosen as the reference
value
1NIF, 2IF

Maybe this helps too.

Clara

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [StatForLing with R] Re: How can I change the reference values in logistic regression?
parts:
Certainly possible, but makes handling of graphs later more difficult
because plotting functions that automatically grab factor levels with
then use these slightly uglier factor levels (e.g., boxplot), which
means you end up having to override those again manually, which makes
for messier and more cumbersome code.

STG
--
Stefan Th. Gries

University of California, Santa Barbara
http://www.linguistics.ucsb.edu/faculty/stgries
-----------------------------------------------
